children: OpenWorld and VerifyMe have completed their business combination, with the combined company trading on Nasdaq under OPNW from October 1.
Management says the company will focus on institutional-grade tokenization of real-world assets.
OpenWorld also intends to pursue a dual listing on Figure OPEN, a blockchain-based trading platform, by November.
A new publicly traded company has entered the real-world asset tokenization race.

OpenWorld completed its business combination with VerifyMe and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker OPNW at the October 1 market open. The combined business is being led by digital-assets executive Matthew Shaw and is positioning institutional-grade tokenization as a core part of its strategy.
That makes the transaction more relevant to crypto markets than an ordinary corporate name change. OpenWorld is targeting the infrastructure behind tokenized assets
The company says it wants to help digitise real-world assets rather than launch a single token or consumer trading app.

That puts it inside a rapidly expanding part of the market where traditional securities, private assets and blockchain settlement are beginning to overlap. Tokenization businesses need more than a smart contract. They also need investor records, compliance controls, transfer restrictions, custody connections and secondary-market infrastructure.
OpenWorld’s public listing gives investors a conventional equity route into that theme.

The company also says it intends to pursue a listing on Figure OPEN, a blockchain-based trading platform, with a target of November 2026. That plan is separate from the Nasdaq listing and should not be treated as already completed.

The same convergence is already visible elsewhere in capital markets. The SEC’s wider crypto rulemaking agenda is trying to give tokenised assets clearer legal pathways, while the agency is also considering how advisers and regulated funds should hold digital assets. At the trading level, 24-hour market infrastructure is making traditional securities look more like the always-on markets crypto introduced years ago. Public-market tokenization companies are still an early category
The opportunity is large, but the sector remains messy.

“Real-world assets” can mean everything from tokenized Treasury bills and private credit to shares, property interests and collectibles. Companies entering the space will need to prove that blockchain settlement produces a real operational advantage rather than just a new wrapper around existing assets.

That is why projects linking conventional capital-market plumbing to onchain execution are getting more attention. NewsBTC has also covered the growth of institutional OTC crypto activity, another part of the market where traditional and crypto-native infrastructure are merging. The merger is complete; the strategy still has to be executed
OpenWorld is now a Nasdaq-listed company. That part is done.
The harder work begins after the ticker change: building regulated tokenization products, attracting issuers and investors, and turning a broad RWA thesis into revenue.

For crypto markets, OPNW is worth watching less because another company has changed its name and more because tokenization now has another publicly traded vehicle trying to build the rails underneath it.
This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: OpenWorld Begins Nasdaq Trading As VerifyMe Deal Creates Public Tokenization Company
